title: US inflation hits highest since May after prices climb 3.8% over the last year
summary: Rise occurs amid soaring energy prices, according to last inflation reading before a crucial Fed board meeting The sell-off in US tech stocks continued on Wednesday as investors reacted to continued concern over the AI trade and fresh data that showed inflation jumped in October. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index was down over 4% on Wednesday morning, while the S&P 500 had lost over 2.5% and the Dow had dropped about 2%. By the end of the day the tech-heavy index was down 0.6%, the S&P had lost 0.25% and the Dow managed a small gain of 0.33%. Continue reading...

title: Democrats must unite on AI regulation. Here’s our three-point plan | Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier
summary: Voters are demanding action on the issue. We need to make AI work for the American public, not the tech oligarchs This month’s elections demonstrated the American public’s urgent demand for change. But they also revealed a glaring problem for the Democrats’ policy agenda: they haven’t presented a compelling plan around AI. This is important, because AI isn’t just a political issue in itself: it’s also a primary force behind both the economic disruption and political corruption that drove so many voters to the polls. Continue reading...
authors: Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier

title: We’re in a flaking epidemic. No wonder no one wants to host gatherings | Chelsea Flagan
summary: We point to self-care as we skip out on activities – but routinely staying home poses its own risk to our mental health You might have heard by now, but Americans are quite lonely , especially if they’re young. The kind of low-effort, high-frequency hanging out we used to rely on – dropping by for dinner, meeting up at the park, watching each other’s kids – has all but evaporated from our lives, leaving us unmoored from the social fabric that underpins our most basic wellbeing. (For reference, chronic loneliness has a comparable impact on long-term health to smoking .) Continue reading...

title: Our ‘Paris manifesto’ proposes how to deal with extreme wealth in the AI age | Open letter
summary: It is possible for democracy to reverse the dynamic of oligarchy. But we must act now The explosion of extreme wealth in the world is the defining social fact of our times. When Forbes magazine began ranking the world’s largest fortunes in 1987, the wealth of the richest 0.0001% of our planet’s population equaled 3% of global GDP. Since that time, the wealth held by this tiny group of people – just 3,000 households – has ballooned and now reaches 17% of global GDP. Continue reading...

title: 53 incoming House Democrats to boycott Harvard orientation in support of graduate students’ strike
summary: ‘We have been informed that to attend your event we would be required to cross a union picket line,’ the Democrats say US politics live – latest updates Fifty-three newly elected members of Congress told Harvard University on Tuesday that they will boycott an informal orientation program at Harvard’s Kennedy School next month in support of the school’s striking graduate students union . In a letter to the university’s administrators, the incoming House Democrats expressed thanks for their invitations to the Bipartisan Program for Newly Elected Members of Congress, in which more than 800 members have participated since 1972. title: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame
summary: The job of Mauricio Pochettino’s successor is to fine-tune a team on the up. That requires a bureaucrat rather than a figurehead First, let’s get the Pep Exception out of the way. Or perhaps we’d better call it the Guardiola Caveat. Regardless, the point is the same. If US Soccer can get Pep Guardiola to manage the United States men’s national team, it should. Because when you have the chance to employ the most successful and influential coach of his generation, the thinker who stands upstream of essentially every major tactical current of the last two decades, you just have to do it. But let us assume that US Soccer can’t appoint Guardiola, because he is only a few months into his post-Manchester City sabbatical and still busying himself defending his body of work . Because he has given no recent indication that he wants the job, even though he spent a previous break between managerial gigs living in New York City and was probably only being supportive of his newly-appointed colleague Mauricio Pochettino when he called the project “fascinating” two years ago. Also because he has only ever signed on to coach teams stacked with Ballon d’Or contenders, posing a Phil Jackson-type, bar-room question over whether he would still be exceptional in charge of unexceptional players. Then again, Guardiola says he expects his next job to be in international management, if and when he does return. Continue reading...

title: Beaver supermoon lights up skylines around the world – video
summary: A stunning supermoon rose over skylines around the world. Supermoons occur when the full moon coincides with the moon being at or near its closest point to Earth, making it appear larger than usual. The November full moon is also known as the beaver moon, a name thought to date to when hunters traditionally set traps for beavers in autumn to secure a supply of warm fur for the winter Continue reading...

title: Vance says Jensen Huang doesn’t need pardon after Trump says ‘it’s an option’
summary: Vice-president says he supports reinstatement of Nvidia CEO after ‘assurances’ from top US officials was ‘under no investigation’ JD Vance said on Wednesday that Jensen Huang , the recently reinstalled Nvidia CEO , was never under criminal investigation and therefore did not need a pardon after Donald Trump said he would be open to offering one to the tech executive. The vice-president told reporters he supported Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO after receiving “assurances” from the attorney general and other top US officials that Huang was “under no investigation”.
